breakingChanges.title: BinaryFormatter fully removed
breakingChanges.description: BinaryFormatter is fully removed in .NET 10. It was disabled by default since .NET 7 and flagged as obsolete. Any usage will cause a build or runtime failure.

fix.summary: Replace BinaryFormatter with System.Text.Json or Newtonsoft.Json serialization.
notes: If the type uses [Serializable] attribute, replace with [JsonSerializable] or remove it.
If properties are non-public, use JsonInclude or a custom converter.
For binary performance-critical paths, consider System.Text.Json with Utf8JsonWriter or MessagePack.

breakingChanges.title: Azure Functions in-process model unsupported
breakingChanges.description: The Azure Functions in-process hosting model is not supported on .NET 10. All functions must use the isolated worker model.
breakingChanges._note: Patterns target in-process-specific code only. [FunctionName( is the in-process attribute; isolated worker uses [Function(. Microsoft.Azure.WebJobs package name is intentionally excluded — it appears in isolated worker projects too (e.g. via Extensions.ServiceBus).

fix.summary: Port from in-process model to isolated worker model.

before.label: Program.cs (in-process)

after.label: Program.cs (isolated worker)

additionalChanges.before:
[FunctionName("MyFunc")]
public async Task Run([ServiceBusTrigger("queue")] string msg, ILogger log) { }

breakingChanges.title: Nullable reference type warnings become errors
breakingChanges.description: Projects with <Nullable>enable</Nullable> and <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors> will fail the build. Nullable analysis is stricter in .NET 10 / C# 14.

fix.summary: Add null checks, use null-forgiving operator where safe, or update type declarations.

cases.description: Converting null literal or possible null value to non-nullable type.
Dereference of a possibly null reference.
Non-nullable property must contain non-null value when exiting constructor.
cases.before: public class MyClass { public string Name { get; set; } }

breakingChanges.title: Ambiguous overload resolution (C# 14)
breakingChanges.description: New overloads added in .NET 10 / C# 14 can cause previously unambiguous calls to become ambiguous, especially with null arguments or implicit conversions.

fix.summary: Use explicit cast or named parameters to disambiguate.

after.code:
DoThing((string?)null);   // explicit cast
Logger.Log(message: GetMessage());  // named parameter

breakingChanges.title: Globalization — ICU mode default on Windows
breakingChanges.description: In .NET 10, ICU globalization is the default on Windows (it was NLS before). This can cause changed string comparison, sorting, and casing behaviour for culture-sensitive operations.

fix.summary: Temporarily restore NLS behaviour, then plan to audit culture-sensitive code for ICU compatibility.
fix.longTermFix: Audit all string comparisons. Use StringComparison.Ordinal or StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase where culture-sensitivity is not required. Where culture-sensitivity is needed, verify behaviour under ICU.

breakingChanges.title: AspNetCore framework-included packages
breakingChanges.description: Several Microsoft.AspNetCore.* packages are now included directly in the net10.0 SDK and must not be referenced explicitly in .csproj files.

fix.summary: Remove explicit PackageReference entries for these packages. They ship with the SDK.

after.code: <!-- Remove both lines — these are included in net10.0 SDK -->

breakingChanges.title: Swashbuckle / Swagger compatibility
breakingChanges.description: Swashbuckle.AspNetCore may not have a .NET 10 compatible release at launch. The built-in Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi (available from .NET 9) is the recommended replacement.

fix.summary: Replace Swashbuckle with Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi and scalar or the built-in OpenAPI endpoint.

breakingChanges.title: HttpClient / SocketsHttpHandler default changes
breakingChanges.description: Default connection pool and timeout settings in SocketsHttpHandler have changed in .NET 10. Applications relying on default timeouts or connection limits may see different behaviour.

fix.summary: Explicitly configure PooledConnectionLifetime, ConnectTimeout, and PooledConnectionIdleTimeout if your application is sensitive to these defaults.

breakingChanges.title: Reflection emit APIs removed or sealed
breakingChanges.description: Some Reflection.Emit APIs used for runtime code generation have been removed or had their behaviour changed in .NET 10 as part of the Native AOT and trimming improvements.

fix.summary: Audit reflection emit usage. Consider using source generators or compiled expressions as a more AOT-compatible alternative.
alternatives: Roslyn Source Generators — for compile-time code generation
System.Linq.Expressions — for dynamic expression trees (still supported)
FastExpressionCompiler — NuGet alternative for expression compilation

breakingChanges.title: LINQ overload resolution changes
breakingChanges.description: New LINQ overloads in .NET 10 (e.g. for CountBy, AggregateBy, Index) can cause previously valid calls to become ambiguous when using method groups or lambda overloads.

fix.summary: Add explicit type parameters or cast lambda arguments to disambiguate LINQ calls.

breakingChanges.title: WPF — net10.0-windows TFM required
breakingChanges.description: WPF projects must use the net10.0-windows TFM, not net10.0. Missing the -windows suffix causes a build failure because WPF APIs are Windows-only.

fix.summary: Ensure the TargetFramework includes -windows suffix for all WPF projects.

breakingChanges.title: WPF — third-party control library compatibility
breakingChanges.description: Third-party WPF control libraries (Telerik, DevExpress, Syncfusion, Infragistics, ActiPro) may not have .NET 10 compatible releases available at migration time.

fix.summary: Check vendor release notes for .NET 10 support before upgrading WPF projects.
checklist: If no .NET 10 release available: multi-target (net9.0-windows;net10.0-windows) until vendor supports it

breakingChanges.title: NuGet PackageReference floating version behaviour
breakingChanges.description: Floating version resolution (e.g. 8.0.*) behaves slightly differently in .NET 10 / NuGet 6.x+. Ranges that previously resolved may now resolve to a different version or fail.

fix.summary: Replace floating version ranges with explicit versions after running dotnet-outdated.

breakingChanges.title: System.Text.Json — stricter nullable serialization
breakingChanges.description: System.Text.Json in .NET 10 enforces stricter handling of nullable reference types during serialization and deserialization. Properties marked non-nullable that receive null JSON values will throw by default.

fix.summary: Mark nullable properties with ? or configure JsonSerializerOptions to handle nullability.

breakingChanges.title: Microsoft.Extensions.* version alignment
breakingChanges.description: Microsoft.Extensions.* packages (DependencyInjection, Logging, Hosting, Configuration, etc.) must be updated to version 10.x.x to align with .NET 10. Mixing v8/v9 packages with net10.0 TFM causes version conflict warnings or build errors.

breakingChanges.title: Application Insights 3.x telemetry API shape changes
breakingChanges.description: Upgrading Microsoft.ApplicationInsights to 3.x can break wrappers that relied on older event/exception overloads or attached numeric metrics directly to EventTelemetry or ExceptionTelemetry instances.

fix.summary: Use TelemetryClient overloads that accept name/properties or exception/properties, and emit numeric values separately via TrackMetric.
notes: Prefer TrackEvent(string, IDictionary<string,string>) for event properties.
Prefer TrackException(Exception, IDictionary<string,string>) for exception properties.
Use TrackMetric for numeric telemetry values instead of attaching them to EventTelemetry or ExceptionTelemetry.
